frames.title: Reading · An academic text and summary

blocks.title: Meaning as Use: Wittgenstein’s Later Turn
paras: In the *Philosophical Investigations* (published posthumously in 1953), Wittgenstein **abandons** the picture theory of meaning **advanced** in his earlier *Tractatus*. **According to** the later view, the meaning of a word **is not** an object it names but **its use** in a **language-game**. Words, he **suggests**, **resemble** members of a family: no single feature **runs through** them all, yet they are **linked** by overlapping similarities.

**Wittgenstein contends** that philosophical puzzles **arise** when language **goes on holiday**, that is, when words are **detached** from the **practices** that give them sense. The task of philosophy is therefore **therapeutic**: **to bring** words **back** from their metaphysical to their **everyday** use. **Summary:** meaning is not **behind** words; it is **in** what we do with them.

items.q: Wittgenstein later says meaning is an object that a word names.
items.why: is not an object it names.

items.q: The text says Wittgenstein wrote the Tractatus in prison.

blocks.body: Um bom **resumo** mantém a ideia central, usa **verbos de atribuição** precisos e **não copia** frases inteiras. Em leitura técnica, o ritmo é regular, com pausas antes de termos-chave (*language-game*).
*Contend* (sustentar) ≠ *content* (conteúdo/contente). *Suggest* não se usa com *to + pessoa*: *He suggests that…* ✓.

items.s: Wittgenstein ___ that puzzles arise when language goes on holiday. (contend)
___ to the later view, meaning is use. (according)
Meaning is not behind words; it is ___ what we do. (in)

body: **Go on holiday.** — Sair de férias (linguagem).
**Run through.** — Atravessar.
**Lie in.** — Residir em.
**Boil down to.** — Resumir-se a.
**In a nutshell.** — Em poucas palavras.
**Bring back to.** — Trazer de volta a.
**Make sense of.** — Dar sentido a.
**In other words.** — Em outras palavras.
**Put it simply.** — Dito de forma simples.
**The long and short of it.** — Resumindo.
**How would you summarise the later view?** — Como você resumiria a visão tardia?
**And what does “family resemblance” suggest?** — E o que “semelhança de família” sugere?
**According to Wittgenstein, meaning is use in a language-game.** — Segundo Wittgenstein, significado é uso num jogo de linguagem.

blocks.title: Study session
lines: How would you summarise the later view?
Como você resumiria a visão tardia?
According to Wittgenstein, meaning is use in a language-game.
Segundo Wittgenstein, significado é uso num jogo de linguagem.
E o que “semelhança de família” sugere?
That no single feature runs through all uses of a word.
Que nenhum traço único atravessa todos os usos de uma palavra.

items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.

I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence summary of an academic idea you know, using According to…, two attribution verbs and a final summary sentence.
blocks.model: According to the author, memory is reconstructive rather than archival. She contends that each recall alters the trace. Studies suggest that confidence does not guarantee accuracy. The text resembles a warning: trust, but verify. Summary: remembering is making, not retrieving.

items.q: What does “picture theory of meaning” mean?
items.why: **picture theory of meaning** = teoria figurativa do significado.
